summary: Iter11 backend verification of admin_analytics tz-naive datetime bug fix (server.py L1994-L2004). Wrote new test_iter11_analytics.py with 4 targeted tests including seeding a tz-NAIVE updated_at row in payment_transactions to reproduce the exact iter9/iter10 crash condition. ALL 4/4 iter11 tests PASS: (1) unauthed → 401, (2) authed with seeded tz-naive donation row → 200 with all 11 required JSON keys present, donations_count>=1, donations_cents>=1234 (proves tz-naive row is compared safely and counted), (3) days=7 → window_days=7, (4) days=90 → window_days=90. Re-ran iter9 regression suite: 13/13 PASS (previously 10/13 with 3 admin_analytics failures). Fix is correct: `upd_aware = upd if upd.tzinfo else upd.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` normalizes before comparing to tz-aware cutoff.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L1998-L2003 — tz normalization is applied only inside isinstance(upd, datetime) branch. If updated_at is stored as ISO string (as paid_at is on line 1992), rows would be silently skipped. Current DB rows use datetime objects so it works, but worth confirming write path is consistent. Not blocking.

Endpoint is named /admin/analytics but has no admin gate — any authed user reads global business metrics (order totals, donor emails, signup counts). Product intent may be admin-only; noted in iter9/10 too. Not part of this fix scope.
test_credentials: Ephemeral: user 'test-user-iter11-<ts>' + session token 'test_session_iter11_<ts>', both cleaned up in fixture teardown.
seed_data_creation: 1 tz-naive payment_transactions donation row + 1 user + 1 session; all deleted post-test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter11 tz-datetime fix is verified end-to-end. The previously-failing 3 admin_analytics tests in test_iter9.py now pass alongside the new dedicated tz-naive repro test. No open backend issues from this fix. Test file test_iter11_analytics.py is a regression asset for future iterations.
rca of the issue: RCA: db.payment_transactions rows have `updated_at` stored as tz-naive datetime (via datetime.utcnow() somewhere in the write path), while `cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=days)` is tz-aware. Python raises TypeError when comparing naive vs aware datetimes with >=. Fix: normalize `upd_aware = upd if upd.tzinfo else upd.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` before comparison. Verified by seeding a tz-naive row and confirming 200 + correct counting.
